name: Boost (step-up) converter
description: Non-isolated step-up converter: inductor at the input, switch to ground, rectifier to the output, feedback network.
typical_input_requirements: Input range (minimum at end of battery)
electrical_characteristics: Vout > Vin; input current = Iout/(1-D)/eta is higher than the output current
Output not isolated from the input at shutdown (diode path) unless a disconnect switch is used
current_power_characteristics: Input current up to several A; 0.1-5 A output
critical_electrical_constraints: Hot loop is switch, diode and Cout: tight
Input current (not output current) sizes the inductor path and input copper
Output over-voltage protection when the load can disconnect
Input disconnect when the application must not leak Vin to the output at shutdown
stackup_recommendations: 2 layers with 2 oz copper for converters above ~3 A; 4 layers with inner ground for controllers with sensitive feedback
Heavy copper (2 oz) when trace width from IPC-2221 exceeds what the board width allows
placement_rules: Minimise the hot loop (input capacitor, high-side switch, low-side switch/diode) area: these three parts touch each other
Inductor adjacent to the switch node pin; switch node copper as small as the current allows
Output capacitor at the inductor output; feedback divider at the controller FB pin, away from the inductor and switch node
Gate driver next to the MOSFET gates; bootstrap capacitor next to the driver
routing_rules: Switch node: short, wide, single layer; never under the feedback network
Feedback trace short and shielded by ground, routed away from the inductor
Power path widths from IPC-2221 for the declared current and temperature rise; polygons for > 3 A
copper_ground_requirements: Power ground and signal ground joined at one point near the controller
Copper pour under the inductor only if the inductor datasheet allows (shielded types)
Thermal vias under MOSFET and diode exposed pads to the opposite-side copper
thermal_considerations: Calculate conduction and switching loss per device; junction temperature at max ambient must stay below the datasheet limit with margin
Copper area per watt from the device datasheet thermal curves; heatsink when the area is not available
emi_emc_considerations: Hot-loop area is the first EMI control; snubber footprint on the switch node
Input pi-filter footprint for conducted emissions when the product is tested to CISPR 32/25
Spread-spectrum or frequency choice to keep harmonics out of sensitive bands
protection_requirements: Input over-voltage and reverse polarity per the application
Over-current/short-circuit protection by the controller; output over-voltage clamp where the load is sensitive
Fuse rating against the input current at minimum input voltage
verification_requirements: Every rail current declared (unknown current blocks routing)
Trace width per net from desk.ipc with declared temperature rise
Voltage drop on the output path within the regulation budget
Hot-loop area recorded; DRC with clearance from the highest node voltage
manufacturing_constraints: 2 oz copper option recorded in the manufacturer profile; minimum width/clearance from the fabricator table for the chosen copper weight
Large pads on magnetics: solder mask defined; thermal relief decision explicit
unsupported_conditions: Output short-circuit without a disconnect switch (boost cannot limit it)
Inductor rated for output current instead of input current

maturity.evidence: rule set evaluated against synthetic fixtures in tests/test_cross_domain_cases.py
